candidates.source_name: 1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) / Book of the Watchers (1 Enoch 1-36)
candidates.draft_body:
1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Book of the Watchers (1 Enoch 1-36) (c. 200 BC)

'And there I saw the ends of the earth whereon the heaven rests, and the portals of the heaven open. And I saw how the stars of heaven come forth, and I counted the portals out of which they proceed' — Enoch's vision of the cosmological mechanism by which stars rise and set. The 'portals' (Geez bāʾəw) are gates in the heavenly dome through which the heavenly bodies pass on their appointed circuits. Tewahedo theological cosmology preserves this gateway-cosmology in its liturgical hymnody: the doxologies frequently reference the 'portals of heaven' through which prayers ascend and divine gifts descend.
